tuples.mechanism: publishing one text at a realm's edges tells officials the centre is watching
tuples.evidence_lens: wording compared between copies at widely separated sites

tuples.episode_object: a polished sandstone pillar with a carved capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Ganges plain, the mid third century BCE
tuples.mechanism: quarrying and hauling monoliths hundreds of miles demonstrates logistics as much as piety
tuples.evidence_lens: stone traced by petrography to a single quarry region

tuples.episode_object: a bilingual inscription in Greek and Aramaic
tuples.time_place_scope: Kandahar in southern Afghanistan, the third century BCE
tuples.mechanism: translating a royal message into local administrative languages admits one tongue's limits
tuples.evidence_lens: the two versions compared for what each adds or omits

tuples.episode_object: an edict naming a war and its human cost
tuples.mechanism: a ruler publicising his own war's cost converts conquest into a reason for restraint
tuples.evidence_lens: the stated figures weighed against what the region's sites can support

tuples.episode_object: a cave chamber with a polished interior
tuples.time_place_scope: the Barabar hills in Bihar, about 250 BCE
tuples.mechanism: endowing a rival sect's shelter buys quiet from groups the court does not follow
tuples.evidence_lens: dedication inscriptions dated by the regnal years they name

tuples.episode_object: a pillar recording a village's reduced dues
tuples.time_place_scope: Lumbini in the Terai, about 249 BCE
tuples.mechanism: cutting one village's share on a pilgrimage visit makes fiscal favour visible and local
tuples.evidence_lens: the stated share compared with tax terms in other early sources

tuples.episode_object: a pillar carrying an order against schism
tuples.time_place_scope: Sarnath near Varanasi, the third century BCE
tuples.mechanism: backing one monastic ruling with royal officers puts a state inside a religious dispute
tuples.evidence_lens: copies of the order compared for identical clauses across sites

tuples.episode_object: a copper plate about relief from a storehouse
tuples.time_place_scope: Sohgaura in the eastern Ganges plain, the Mauryan period
tuples.mechanism: holding reserve grain against shortage years makes famine a state responsibility
tuples.evidence_lens: the plate's script dated by letter forms against dated inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: a stone slab about district granary stores
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Ganges at Mahasthangarh, the Mauryan period
tuples.mechanism: an outlying province keeping its own reserve shortens the response to a bad harvest
tuples.evidence_lens: the inscription read with excavated storage structures at the site

tuples.episode_object: a punch-marked silver coin from a hoard
tuples.time_place_scope: Taxila on the upper Indus, the Mauryan period
tuples.mechanism: a common punched currency lets revenue move between provinces without conversion
tuples.evidence_lens: punch marks classified and hoards mapped by composition

tuples.episode_object: a wooden palisade preserved in wet ground
tuples.time_place_scope: Pataliputra on the Ganges, the third century BCE
tuples.mechanism: a timber-walled capital shows defence spending that a later century stopped maintaining
tuples.evidence_lens: timbers dated by radiocarbon and compared with visitors' descriptions

tuples.episode_object: a minor edict naming the king in person
tuples.time_place_scope: Maski in the Raichur doab, the third century BCE
tuples.mechanism: using a personal name in one version links an anonymous title to a known ruler
tuples.evidence_lens: the named copy compared with the many that give only the title

tuples.episode_object: a stupa railing carrying donor names
tuples.time_place_scope: Sanchi in central India, the second century BCE
tuples.mechanism: hundreds of small donations show patronage broadening well beyond the court
tuples.evidence_lens: donor inscriptions counted by stated occupation and home town

tuples.episode_object: a rock inscription in a north-western dialect
tuples.time_place_scope: Shahbazgarhi on the north-west frontier, the third century BCE
tuples.mechanism: writing in a regional script keeps a message readable where the court's script is not
tuples.evidence_lens: script and dialect compared across the surviving edict copies

tuples.episode_object: a later ruler's inscription about a dam repair
tuples.time_place_scope: Junagadh in Saurashtra, the second century CE
tuples.mechanism: a much later repair record preserves what an earlier administration built and staffed
tuples.evidence_lens: the later text's claims compared with the earlier edict on the same rock

tuples.episode_object: a treatise on statecraft in manuscript
tuples.time_place_scope: north India, the early centuries CE
tuples.mechanism: a composite manual describes an ideal administration no single reign need have run
tuples.evidence_lens: textual layers separated by language and by internal cross-references

tuples.episode_object: a Greek envoy's report preserved in quotation
tuples.time_place_scope: the Greek-reading Mediterranean, the first century BCE
tuples.mechanism: an outsider's account survives only through later quoting, filtering what reaches us
tuples.evidence_lens: quotations compared where two later authors preserve the same passage

tuples.episode_object: a burnished black pottery bowl
tuples.time_place_scope: Kausambi on the Yamuna, about 250 BCE
tuples.mechanism: a distinctive fine ware spreading with administration maps the reach of officialdom
tuples.evidence_lens: sherd distributions mapped against sites naming imperial officers

tuples.episode_object: a pillar re-erected in a later capital
tuples.mechanism: a later sultan moving a monument keeps an unread text safe for eventual decipherment
tuples.evidence_lens: the transport account in later chronicles compared with the pillar's condition

tuples.episode_object: a coin of a successor dynasty
tuples.mechanism: provinces breaking away first where officers were locally recruited shows what held them
tuples.evidence_lens: coin issues mapped by region to date the loss of central control

tuples.episode_object: a tophet stele cut with a votive dedication and a family name
tuples.time_place_scope: Carthage, North Africa, the sixth century BCE
tuples.mechanism: office-holding families advertise themselves in temple gifts, fixing an oligarchy in stone
tuples.evidence_lens: names and titles on votive stelae counted by stratum across the sanctuary

tuples.episode_object: a victory column faced with the bronze beaks of captured ships
tuples.time_place_scope: western Sicily and the Tyrrhenian sea, the 260s BCE
tuples.mechanism: captured hulls give a land power a template, so a fleet is copied rather than invented
tuples.evidence_lens: Polybius on fleet totals compared with shipshed dimensions excavated at Punic harbours

tuples.episode_object: a bronze warship ram stamped with a magistrate's approval mark
tuples.time_place_scope: the sea off the Aegates islands, 241 BCE
tuples.mechanism: a war financed by loans ends when private lenders stop underwriting replacement hulls
tuples.evidence_lens: recovered rams weighed and their inscriptions collated against recorded subscription loans

tuples.episode_object: a pay tally for unpaid soldiers held in a city treasury
tuples.time_place_scope: Carthage and its Libyan territory, 241-237 BCE
tuples.mechanism: arrears owed to hired troops turn an army into a claimant against the state that raised it
tuples.evidence_lens: coin hoards in the Libyan interior dated to the revolt years and mapped by findspot

tuples.episode_object: a treaty clause surrendering an island and raising an indemnity
tuples.mechanism: a weakened debtor accepts a new demand because refusal restarts a war it cannot fund
tuples.evidence_lens: indemnity figures in the narrative sources checked against silver weights of issued coin

tuples.episode_object: a silver shekel struck at a mint in a newly held mining district
tuples.mechanism: silver from conquered mines pays an army directly, freeing a general from home approval
tuples.evidence_lens: die studies and metal isotope work on Barcid issues traced to Iberian ore sources

tuples.episode_object: a hoard of denarii buried beside a farmstead threshing floor
tuples.time_place_scope: the Po valley and central Italy, 218-216 BCE
tuples.mechanism: battlefield defeat strips a state of field armies but not of allied manpower reserves
tuples.evidence_lens: burial dates of coin hoards plotted against the recorded line of march

tuples.episode_object: a city charter granting a defecting town its own laws
tuples.mechanism: an invader must outbid the incumbent's terms, or allied cities will not change sides
tuples.evidence_lens: surviving terms offered to defected towns compared with their pre-war obligations

tuples.episode_object: an olive press and storage jars in a burnt rural estate
tuples.time_place_scope: the Bagradas valley, North Africa, 204-202 BCE
tuples.mechanism: an enemy landing in the home countryside recalls the field army and cedes the initiative
tuples.evidence_lens: destruction layers at rural sites dated by imported pottery across the valley

tuples.episode_object: a ratified peace text limiting warships and requiring hostages
tuples.mechanism: a ban on waging war without permission hands a neighbour a lever it can pull at will
tuples.evidence_lens: treaty terms as transmitted compared across Polybius, Livy and Appian

tuples.episode_object: an audit of harbour dues and temple revenues
tuples.mechanism: recovered revenue repays an indemnity early, which alarms the creditor more than default would
tuples.evidence_lens: recorded indemnity instalments set beside the city's known customs income

tuples.episode_object: a marker dividing a kingdom's grazing land from a city's fields
tuples.time_place_scope: the Numidian border districts, the 160s-150s BCE
tuples.mechanism: an arbiter who profits from one side's raids has no reason to settle a border dispute
tuples.evidence_lens: repeated border arbitrations counted and their outcomes tabulated by beneficiary

tuples.episode_object: a senatorial decree authorising an army to sail
tuples.mechanism: a rival's visible recovery reframes a beaten state as a future threat rather than a client
tuples.evidence_lens: senatorial debate as reported by Appian read against the timing of the last indemnity payment

tuples.episode_object: a receipt for surrendered armour and catapults
tuples.time_place_scope: Utica and the bay of Tunis, 149 BCE
tuples.mechanism: escalating demands work only after disarmament removes the means to refuse them
tuples.evidence_lens: the sequence of Roman demands in 149 reconstructed from Appian and Polybian fragments

tuples.episode_object: a triple line of ditch and rampart cut across an isthmus
tuples.mechanism: a siege wall across the land approach shifts the contest to who can close the sea lane
tuples.evidence_lens: siege lines described in the sources compared with the surveyed isthmus topography

tuples.episode_object: a collapsed house wall sealing burnt grain and household pottery
tuples.mechanism: street fighting in dense housing makes demolition the only way an attacker can advance
tuples.evidence_lens: the burnt horizon on the hill excavated and dated by its imported wares

tuples.episode_object: the dressed stone quays and shipsheds of a circular naval basin
tuples.time_place_scope: the twin harbours of Carthage, the second century BCE
tuples.mechanism: a fleet base sized for scores of hulls is read by a rival as intent, not as inheritance
tuples.evidence_lens: shipshed counts and berth widths measured in the excavated naval harbour

tuples.episode_object: an inventory of temple statues removed from a sacked Greek city
tuples.mechanism: two exemplary sackings in one year teach every watching city the cost of resistance
tuples.evidence_lens: Greek and Roman accounts of 146 compared for what each treats as the deterrent

tuples.episode_object: a ditch dug to mark the outer limit of a new province
tuples.time_place_scope: the North African coast under Roman administration, after 146 BCE
tuples.mechanism: a surveyed boundary turns conquest into a tax district with named liable communities
tuples.evidence_lens: the provincial boundary ditch traced by survey and matched to later tribute lists

tuples.episode_object: a bronze survey map dividing farmland into squared lots
tuples.time_place_scope: Roman Africa, the first century BCE
tuples.mechanism: squared allotments resettle citizens on seized land, making the seizure hard to reverse
tuples.evidence_lens: centuriation grids visible in aerial photography over the Bagradas plain

coverage_profiles.subject: the fall of the Roman Republic

tuples.episode_object: a boundary stone reset on public land by a land commission
tuples.mechanism: a commission with power to survey and reassign land makes tenure itself a political prize
tuples.evidence_lens: surviving land-commission boundary stones mapped against known public land

tuples.episode_object: an estate inventory listing field slaves and their daily tasks
tuples.time_place_scope: the Italian countryside, the second century BCE
tuples.mechanism: slave-worked estates undercut smallholders, and displaced farmers stop appearing in the levy
tuples.evidence_lens: field survey counts of small farm sites against large villa sites through the period

tuples.episode_object: a military levy register opened to men without property
tuples.time_place_scope: Numidia and the North African frontier, 112-105 BCE
tuples.mechanism: recruits with no land to return to look to a commander, not the treasury, for a pension
tuples.evidence_lens: property qualifications in the levy tracked through successive recorded enrolments

tuples.episode_object: a bronze tablet granting citizenship to an allied community
tuples.time_place_scope: Rome and the Italian allied towns, 91-88 BCE
tuples.mechanism: extending the franchise ends a revolt but multiplies the voters a single patron can mobilise
tuples.evidence_lens: citizenship grants counted by community and set beside later voting-tribe assignments

tuples.episode_object: a tax-farming contract for a province's revenues
tuples.mechanism: revenue sold to private syndicates makes provincial anger a lobby inside the capital
tuples.evidence_lens: publicani contract terms in Cicero's speeches compared with recorded provincial complaints

tuples.episode_object: a marching order that names the capital as the objective
tuples.mechanism: an army loyal to its general treats the city as a target once his command is revoked
tuples.evidence_lens: the sequence of commands revoked and restored traced through the annalistic tradition

tuples.episode_object: a posted list of names whose property was forfeit
tuples.mechanism: confiscation rewards the winner's supporters, so each victory manufactures its own faction
tuples.evidence_lens: proscription lists and later ownership of confiscated estates traced in legal speeches

tuples.episode_object: an iron slave collar and fetters from a training barracks
tuples.mechanism: a rural slave majority means any internal revolt pulls field armies back from the frontier
tuples.evidence_lens: estate slave numbers estimated from villa storage capacity in the affected districts

tuples.episode_object: a law conferring a sweeping command over sea and coast
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Mediterranean and Syria, 67-63 BCE
tuples.mechanism: an extraordinary command concentrates fleets, funds and clients in one man for years
tuples.evidence_lens: terms of the pirate and eastern commands compared with ordinary consular provinces

tuples.episode_object: a senate resolution authorising emergency measures against citizens
tuples.mechanism: an emergency decree lets the senate kill citizens untried, and the precedent outlives it
tuples.evidence_lens: invocations of the emergency decree counted and their legal aftermaths compared

tuples.episode_object: a campaign dispatch published in the capital by its author
tuples.mechanism: a general who publishes his own campaign controls the account by which he will be judged
tuples.evidence_lens: Caesar's commentaries compared with Gallic site destruction dated by excavation

tuples.episode_object: a burnt senate house used as a funeral pyre
tuples.time_place_scope: the streets and forum of Rome, the 50s BCE
tuples.mechanism: armed gangs decide assemblies, so elections stop settling anything and offices go unfilled
tuples.evidence_lens: years with delayed or failed consular elections counted across the decade

tuples.episode_object: a legion's standards carried across a provincial boundary river
tuples.mechanism: crossing a command boundary under arms converts a legal dispute into a civil war
tuples.evidence_lens: provincial boundaries of the period reconstructed from surviving grant legislation

tuples.episode_object: scattered sling bullets and camp ditches on a battlefield plain
tuples.mechanism: one decisive engagement removes the senatorial army, leaving no body able to command
tuples.evidence_lens: the battlefield's camp works surveyed and compared with the deployments described

tuples.episode_object: a grain shipment redirected from a provincial harbour
tuples.time_place_scope: Egypt and the eastern provinces, 48-47 BCE
tuples.mechanism: control of the grain provinces feeds the capital, and whoever feeds it is not easily refused
tuples.evidence_lens: routes and harbour capacity for the grain fleets reconstructed from wreck finds

tuples.episode_object: a calendar reformed to a fixed solar year
tuples.mechanism: a ruler who fixes the calendar shows that priestly and civil offices now answer to one man
tuples.evidence_lens: dating formulas in inscriptions before and after the reform compared for authority named

tuples.episode_object: a deed transferring a farm to a discharged soldier
tuples.mechanism: settling veterans on seized Italian land buys an army and creates a class that fears reversal
tuples.evidence_lens: veteran colony charters compared with earlier ownership recorded in the same districts

tuples.episode_object: a legion's donative paid out in freshly minted silver
tuples.mechanism: rival heirs bid for the same troops, so pay rises until only plunder can meet the promises
tuples.evidence_lens: silver output of the civil war mints estimated from surviving dies and hoards

tuples.episode_object: oar-bench fittings recovered from a naval battle site
tuples.time_place_scope: the Ionian sea off western Greece, 31 BCE
tuples.mechanism: a blockaded fleet loses rowers to desertion and disease before it loses a battle
tuples.evidence_lens: campaign supply positions reconstructed from harbour and camp sites in the region

tuples.episode_object: a golden shield and wreath voted for a ruler and set in the senate house
tuples.mechanism: keeping the old offices while one man holds them all disguises the change of regime
tuples.evidence_lens: honours of the settlement listed in the ruler's own record and in later coin legends

coverage_profiles.subject: the collapse of the Han dynasty

tuples.episode_object: a state iron foundry's mould stamped with an office name
tuples.time_place_scope: Chang'an, the western Han capital, the first century BCE
tuples.mechanism: state monopolies fund armies but push tool costs onto the farmers who must buy them
tuples.evidence_lens: foundry stamps and tool quality compared between monopoly and private workshops

tuples.episode_object: a breached dyke and a silted canal bed

tuples.mechanism: an unmaintained channel floods the tax heartland, and refugees become an armed population
tuples.evidence_lens: flood layers in floodplain stratigraphy dated against recorded dyke repairs

tuples.episode_object: an edict recalling coinage and reviving archaic currency forms
tuples.mechanism: repeated currency reform destroys confidence, so metal is hoarded and cloth becomes money
tuples.evidence_lens: coin hoards of the interregnum studied for composition and burial date

tuples.episode_object: a granary account left unbalanced in a plundered county office
tuples.time_place_scope: Shandong and the eastern plain, 17-27 CE
tuples.mechanism: an army that cannot be paid lives off the counties it crosses, spreading the shortage it fled
tuples.evidence_lens: county granary capacities in the eastern plain set against recorded relief distributions

tuples.episode_object: a founding proclamation restoring dynastic titles and offices
tuples.mechanism: a restoration that rewards magnate allies concedes land and men it can never later tax
tuples.evidence_lens: landholding recorded for founding families compared with household registers of the era

tuples.episode_object: a watchtower's wooden slips recording garrison rations
tuples.time_place_scope: the Ordos and the northern frontier, the first century CE
tuples.mechanism: frontier garrisons paid from the interior fail first when interior transport breaks down
tuples.evidence_lens: dated wooden slips from frontier posts read for ration and pay entries over time

tuples.episode_object: a tomb model of a fortified manor with its own watchtower
tuples.time_place_scope: the Sichuan basin, the first century CE
tuples.mechanism: great estates that fortify and arm their tenants remove those households from the tax rolls
tuples.evidence_lens: manor models and estate tomb goods compared with the falling registered population

tuples.episode_object: a household register listing families county by county
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Yangzi, the first and second centuries CE
tuples.mechanism: recorded population falls where households flee to estates, shrinking the taxable base
tuples.evidence_lens: census totals by commandery compared between the surviving Han registers

tuples.episode_object: a palace memorial appointing a regent from an empress's family
tuples.mechanism: child emperors put power with consort kin and eunuchs, so succession becomes a palace contest
tuples.evidence_lens: ages at accession and regency arrangements tabulated across the later reigns

tuples.episode_object: an evacuation order relocating a frontier commandery's offices
tuples.time_place_scope: the Han commanderies of the north-west, the 100s-140s CE
tuples.mechanism: abandoning a frontier district moves the war inland and turns loyal auxiliaries into raiders
tuples.evidence_lens: commandery seats relocated in the geographical treatises and matched to site abandonment

tuples.episode_object: a list of banned officials excluded from holding office
tuples.mechanism: barring a whole faction from service leaves only palace clients to staff the government
tuples.evidence_lens: proscribed names in the histories cross-checked against later appointment records

tuples.episode_object: a healing talisman burnt and dissolved into water
tuples.mechanism: a religious movement supplies the network, treasury and discipline a rising otherwise lacks
tuples.evidence_lens: the movement's spread mapped from the commanderies named in the rebellion accounts

tuples.episode_object: a roadside charity lodge stocked with grain and meat
tuples.time_place_scope: Hanzhong and the upper Han river, the 190s CE
tuples.mechanism: a sect that governs a valley collects tithes and gives justice, replacing the county office
tuples.evidence_lens: the sect's recorded administration compared with the county structure it displaced

tuples.episode_object: a palace gate forced open during a night attack
tuples.mechanism: destroying the eunuch establishment leaves the capital's only armed force a frontier general
tuples.evidence_lens: the composition of capital garrisons before and after the year of the palace killings

tuples.episode_object: a mint striking small thin coins of reduced weight
tuples.time_place_scope: Chang'an and the Wei valley, 190-195 CE
tuples.mechanism: coin cut to a fraction of its old weight makes grain and silk the real money of the provinces
tuples.evidence_lens: weights of dated Han coin issues plotted against recorded grain prices

tuples.episode_object: a supply depot burnt during a campaign on the northern plain
tuples.mechanism: warlord contests turn on granaries, so the side that can store longer outlasts the other
tuples.evidence_lens: recorded army sizes checked against the carrying capacity of the campaign routes

tuples.episode_object: river craft chained together for a crossing
tuples.mechanism: a river frontier a northern army cannot cross freezes the split into three durable states
tuples.evidence_lens: naval capacity of the southern regimes inferred from shipyard and timber records

tuples.episode_object: a colony field register assigning soldiers to state farmland
tuples.time_place_scope: Xu province and the eastern plain, the 190s-200s CE
tuples.mechanism: settling troops on state farms feeds an army without taxing peasants a warlord cannot reach
tuples.evidence_lens: military colony yields recorded in the histories compared with civilian tax quotas

tuples.episode_object: an abdication document transferring the imperial seals
tuples.mechanism: a formal abdication legitimises a general's regime and hands rivals the same script to copy
tuples.evidence_lens: abdication texts compared with the wording of the later successions that imitate them

tuples.episode_object: three separate reign-title calendars issued in one year
tuples.time_place_scope: Luoyang, Chengdu and Jianye, the 220s CE
tuples.mechanism: rival courts each dating their own year makes any one administration's writ merely regional
tuples.evidence_lens: reign titles on dated inscriptions and tomb bricks mapped by region for the decade

tuples.episode_object: a citizenship grant extended to the free population of the provinces
tuples.mechanism: making everyone a citizen widens the base of the citizen-only taxes and of legal jurisdiction
tuples.evidence_lens: the grant's text on a Giessen papyrus read against later provincial tax records

tuples.episode_object: a legionary fortress granary rebuilt with smaller bays
tuples.mechanism: supply organised locally for each garrison lets frontier armies act without central approval
tuples.evidence_lens: granary floor areas in Rhine forts measured across successive building phases

tuples.episode_object: a milestone recut with a new ruler's name over an erased one
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Danube frontier, the 250s CE
tuples.mechanism: provincial armies proclaim their own emperors, so each frontier gets a candidate and a war
tuples.evidence_lens: milestones with erased and recut imperial names counted along the Danube roads

tuples.episode_object: a legion's dedication slab defaced after a failed proclamation
tuples.time_place_scope: North Africa and the Numidian legionary base, 238 CE
tuples.mechanism: a province backing a losing claimant loses its legion, and the frontier it held goes unwatched
tuples.evidence_lens: erased dedications at the African legionary base dated by the emperors they name

tuples.episode_object: a peace payment weighed out in gold to a neighbouring king
tuples.time_place_scope: the Roman-Persian border in Mesopotamia, the 240s CE
tuples.mechanism: buying off one frontier with bullion drains the coin needed to pay the army on another
tuples.evidence_lens: subsidy sums in the narrative sources compared against gold coin weights of the reigns

tuples.episode_object: a city wall built in haste from reused tombstones and column drums
tuples.mechanism: cities that wall themselves with their own monuments no longer expect relief to arrive
tuples.evidence_lens: reused inscribed blocks in late city walls catalogued and dated by their original texts

tuples.episode_object: a rock relief showing a captured emperor before a mounted king
tuples.mechanism: the capture of a ruler proves a frontier army can be destroyed rather than merely pushed back
tuples.evidence_lens: the Naqsh-e Rostam reliefs read against the Roman narrative accounts of the campaign

tuples.episode_object: a bilingual honorific inscription naming a caravan city's ruler
tuples.time_place_scope: Palmyra and the Syrian desert, 260-272 CE
tuples.mechanism: a trading city with its own cavalry can defend a region the central army has stopped reaching
tuples.evidence_lens: Palmyrene inscriptions dated by their titles and compared with imperial coin issues there

tuples.episode_object: a coin struck for a ruler recognised only in the western provinces
tuples.mechanism: a breakaway command keeps taxes and troops in place, so secession looks like continuity
tuples.evidence_lens: circulation of the Gallic issues mapped by hoard findspots across the western provinces

tuples.episode_object: a fort rebuilt with projecting towers and a narrowed gate
tuples.time_place_scope: Britain and northern Gaul, the 260s-270s CE
tuples.mechanism: defence in depth accepts raids inside the line and aims to trap raiders rather than block them
tuples.evidence_lens: late fort plans compared with second-century types across the northern provinces

tuples.episode_object: a ship's cargo of looted bronze abandoned on a shoreline
tuples.time_place_scope: the Aegean and the Black sea coasts, the 260s CE
tuples.mechanism: seaborne raiding bypasses the land frontier, exposing provinces with no garrison at all
tuples.evidence_lens: coastal destruction layers dated by coin loss at Aegean and Black sea sites

tuples.episode_object: an order moving a province's name to a new district south of a river
tuples.time_place_scope: Dacia north of the Danube, the 270s CE
tuples.mechanism: withdrawing a salient shortens the line to what the remaining army can actually hold
tuples.evidence_lens: the relocated province's garrison and settlement traced in Danube-side epigraphy

tuples.episode_object: a brick-faced wall enclosing a capital that had none
tuples.mechanism: walling the capital admits its safety now rests on masonry, not on distant frontiers
tuples.evidence_lens: brick stamps in the circuit dated and the wall's building rate estimated from them

tuples.episode_object: a tax receipt written on papyrus in a village office
tuples.time_place_scope: the Egyptian Nile valley, the third century CE
tuples.mechanism: prices quoted in ever larger sums show the coin thinning faster than the tax rate rises
tuples.evidence_lens: Egyptian price and wage figures in dated papyri plotted across the century

tuples.episode_object: a burnt layer sealing a market square's paving
tuples.mechanism: a raid reaching an old inland city ends the assumption that interior cities need no walls
tuples.evidence_lens: the destruction horizon in the Athenian agora dated by its coins and pottery

tuples.episode_object: a buried purse of debased silver under a farmhouse floor
tuples.time_place_scope: the Gallic countryside, the third century CE
tuples.mechanism: coin is buried when metal is falling and roads are unsafe, and lost hoards mark flight
tuples.evidence_lens: hoard burial dates and silver fineness plotted together for the western provinces

tuples.episode_object: an imperial mint moved to a city behind the Alpine passes
tuples.time_place_scope: Milan and northern Italy, the 260s-280s CE
tuples.mechanism: shifting mint and court to a road hub puts a ruler within days of two threatened frontiers
tuples.evidence_lens: mint marks on issues traced as the striking centres move north and east

tuples.episode_object: a provincial list dividing old provinces into smaller units
tuples.mechanism: splitting provinces limits how many troops any one governor can turn against the centre
tuples.evidence_lens: the Verona list of provinces compared with second-century provincial boundaries

tuples.episode_object: a stone-cut schedule of maximum prices for goods and wages
tuples.time_place_scope: Nicomedia and the eastern court, 301 CE
tuples.mechanism: capping prices without fixing the coin drives trade off the market and into requisition
tuples.evidence_lens: surviving fragments of the price schedule compared with papyrus market prices of the time
